outcome: Kept narrower usage flags for eight render-only textures. All contributing shader code, resolutions, schedules, precision and filters are unchanged.

implementation.fallback: narrowTextureUsage=0 restores the exact original usage flags for all eight textures.
implementation.scope: Compute and simulation textures keep their existing permissions. Memoryless MSAA/depth remain renderTarget-only. Same render passes and load/store actions.
implementation.mechanismLimit: Narrow usage permits driver-selected lossless compression on supported Apple GPUs; actual compression ratio, DRAM traffic and residency were not measured.
implementation.instrumentation: dumpBloom=1 adds verification-only packed readbacks of all six completed bloom levels. renderTextureUsage reports actual usage.rawValue of HDR, cache and all six bloom textures. Nil-safe reporting handles missing allocations.

validation.sourceScope: No Metal shader sources changed in this optimization. Native build and Python syntax checks passed. The 14-case comparison was rerun after adding checks of actual usage flags. A final nil-safety-only diagnostic edit was built and Metal-validated afterward.
validation.suiteScope: The dedicated 14-case exact comparison and four API/shader-validation launches passed. The dedicated gate is now part of macos/test.sh. The entire historical suite was not rerun for this resource-descriptor change.

interpretation.cpuTradeoff: Eight-run mean thread CPU encoding increased by approximately 0.015 ms default, 0.003 ms stable, and 0.045 ms portrait. Initial four-run portrait increased by 0.082 ms. CPU frequency, driver compression overhead and scheduling were not isolated; retain the measured costs rather than claiming CPU savings.
interpretation.decision: Keep the reproducible GPU improvement with exact output and small absolute CPU encoding increases. No frame-rate, battery-life or energy gain is claimed.

limitations: Only this M1 was measured. Different GPUs and drivers may behave differently.
Ordinary command-buffer timings, 60 warmup and 120 measured frames per run, fixed scene progression and 30-FPS cap. Benchmark instrumentation excluded validation and GPU stage profiling.
The initial four-run portrait p95 was effectively unchanged; the later eight-run portrait p95 improved approximately 1.1%.
Most quality comparisons use deterministic eight-frame states. API validation additionally exercises live-clock frames.
Wall-clock, CPU and GPU measurements are separate and cannot be added into a measured end-to-end saving.
